title: Persatrix Channel Configuration (v0.3.0+)
description: Internal-only schema until v1.0; `$id` may break across v0.x bumps without notice. Per RFC 0011 §A the canonical channel address is derived at runtime as `<channel_type>:<name>` (e.g., `group:planning`); the SQL `channels.id` PK column is a separate concern. DMs open on demand and are not declared here; threads anchor to a parent message and are likewise implicit.

max_channels.description: Global cap on declared named group channels. DMs and threads are not counted.

max_cascade_depth.description: Primary-enforcement cap on the cooperative-path cascade-depth backstop (RFC 0011 amendment 'Cascade-depth wire propagation', PR 2). Default is 5, aligned with the Python dispatcher's `max_cascade_depth` (agents/dispatch.py). The Go loader treats a zero or absent value as 'use the orchestrator default' so the backstop cannot be silently disabled from config (ChannelRouter.SetMaxCascadeDepth ignores non-positive overrides). Negative values are not permitted by the schema so an operator typo surfaces at `make validate` time rather than as a silent fall-back at startup.

floor_control.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2.5 speaker serialization (floor control): candidate responders take the floor one at a time, each reading the prior speaker's reply, instead of replying concurrently and mutually-blind. As of v0.3.6 the resolved default is ON for every declared (group) channel — omit the key to inherit it; set it false to opt a channel back out. Below two responders (e.g. a DM) it is a no-op regardless. The per-turn wait is floor_turn_timeout_seconds.

floor_turn_timeout_seconds.description: Per-speaker turn timeout for floor control (RFC 0030 amendment decision D2): how long the serialized loop waits for one speaker's reply before advancing to the next responder. Distinct from the 5s per-recipient fanout timeout — a floor turn is LLM-latency-bound. Absent uses the 45s default; the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time.

salience_max_channel_members.description: RFC 0030 Tier B (v0.3.8) channel-size cap (TB6 / amendment OQ #4): above this many candidate responders, the agent-side salience bid is skipped entirely and open-floor `participant`/`chair` members fall back to `addressed`-only, keeping a cheap bid × N members bounded on a large channel. Absent uses the 20 default (kept in lock-step with the agent-side DEFAULT_SALIENCE_MAX_CHANNEL_MEMBERS); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time. The resolved value is carried to the agent on the ChannelMessageEvent wire.

members.description: Explicit, auditable membership list. The v0.2-era `members: "all"` shorthand was dropped per RFC 0011.

respond.description: Member disposition (RFC 0030 relevance amendment). Recommended vocabulary: `participant` (joins the open floor — speaks on un-addressed messages, subject to the Tier B salience bid), `chair` (a low-threshold facilitator: a `participant` that clears the salience bid readily and keeps the discussion moving — v0.3.8; it CANNOT close an interaction, convergence is owned by the governance layers, and its Layer 5 moderator hooks are reserved/inert until v0.4.0), `addressed` (speaks only when @-mentioned or replied to), `observer` (never speaks). The legacy values `always`/`when_mentioned`/`never` keep working and map to `participant`/`addressed`/`observer` respectively; the Go loader normalizes the disposition vocabulary back to the legacy three at load time (`chair` → `always` + a low default `threshold`), so the wire `respond_policy` and every downstream reader are unchanged.

threshold.description: Per-disposition salience threshold for the v0.3.8 Tier B relevance bid: an open-floor `participant` only reaches the (expensive) quality turn when its cheap salience bid clears this bar. Only meaningful on an open-floor disposition (`participant`/`chair`/legacy `always`); the Go loader rejects a `threshold` set on `addressed`/`observer`/`when_mentioned`, where no bid runs — a cross-field rule JSON Schema cannot express, so a schema-valid config can still fail to load. Bias-to-silence — an absent/unset threshold biases toward NOT replying on ambiguous open-floor traffic (the conservative default; calibration is post-soak). `chair` members get a low default so they speak readily. Bounded to the `[0, 1]` salience range (salience is clipped to `[0.0, 1.0]` per RFC 0024; mirrors `autonomy.salience_threshold` in agent.schema.json).

messageMetadata.description: Optional metadata bag on the publish payload (POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages → publishMessageRequest.metadata). Carries cross-cutting wire-level fields that are not part of the core message body. Documented here rather than in the channels.yaml config schema because the config file has no metadata of its own — this definition pins the REST publish contract, mirrored on the gRPC side by typed fields on ChannelMessageEvent.

cascade_depth.description: Hop count along the cooperative-path cascade chain (RFC 0011 amendment 'Cascade-depth wire propagation'). Documented operational range is [0, max_cascade_depth] (default cap 5). The schema enforces a lower bound only — values above the cap are accepted and clamped server-side at the orchestrator's publish boundary so a publisher does not need to know the deployment's current cap to compose a payload. Mirrors the typed `int32 cascade_depth = 11` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).

interaction_id.description: RFC 0020 interaction_id of the open Interaction this message belongs to (RFC 0030 deterministic governance layers, v0.3.8). Opaque string token — RFC 0020 §D names it a ULID, but the agent-side implementation mints a uuid4 (agents/memory/interactions.py), so do not assume ULID sortability. Optional: absent is the untracked / pre-v0.3.8 case, which leaves every governance layer (Layer 1 cost ceiling, Layer 2 reply budget, Layer 4 end-of-interaction votes) at its uncapped default, so the field is additive. When a publisher supplies this key the orchestrator lifts it onto the typed `string interaction_id = 17` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto) so the value survives the publish→fanout boundary that has no metadata map. (No publisher populates the key yet — interaction tracking is agent-side; a producer lands in a later PR.)
